translations.text: At the time of midnight the prophetic voice urges us: let us always speak praise to the Lord the Father, and to the Son,
and also to the Holy Spirit; for the perfect Trinity, of one substance, is always to be praised by us.
This hour holds terror, for it was at this time that the destroying angel brought death upon Egypt and wiped out the firstborn.
This hour is salvation for the righteous, whom the angel there did not dare to punish then, because he feared the sign of the blood.
Egypt wept bitterly over the grim deaths of its children; Israel alone rejoiced, protected by the blood of the lamb.
But we are the people of Israel. We rejoice in you, Lord, scorning the enemy and evil, protected by the blood of Christ.
This is indeed the very time at which, according to the voice of the Gospel, the bridegroom is believed to be coming, the [?] creator of the heavenly kingdom.
The holy virgins run out to meet his coming, carrying bright lamps and rejoicing with great gladness.
But the foolish ones, who have extinguished lamps, are left behind. They knock at the door in vain, for the gate of the kingdom is already shut.
Let us keep faithful watch, carrying bright minds, so that we may worthily run out to meet the coming Saviour.
At the middle hour of the night, Paul and Silas, bound in prison, were praising Christ together, and they were set free.
For us this world is a prison. We praise you, Christ God: loosen the bonds of sin for those who believe in you, Christ.
Holy King, make us worthy of the glory of the coming kingdom, so that we may earn the right to sing your praise together in eternal praises.
God, you who are the light of heaven and the sower of light, who with your shining right hand spread out and open the heaven, upheld by the Father's arm:
Dawn now covers the stars, raising up the red flood, and with moist breezes it baptizes the earth with dew.
The morning star now calls for his chariot, with its rays as spokes and its flaming wheels, so that as he climbs the heights of heaven he knows no delay on his journey.
Now the shadow of night is left behind, darkness leaves the sky, and the morning star, a figure of Christ, wakes the sleeping day.
You are the holy day of days and of light, and you yourself are the light. You are one, mighty over all, almighty, mighty in one Trinity.
We now beseech you, Saviour, and to you we bend the knee. With all our voices we pray to the Father together with the Holy Spirit.
Father, you who hold the heavens, let us now sing your name. May your kingdom come, and may your will also be done.
This saying, your will, has been handed to us to carry out: to be faithful and believing in spirit while the body remains chaste.
Give us our daily bread to eat from you. Forgive us our debts, just as we forgive ours.
Do not let us be led into deceitful temptation, but as we pray with a pure heart, deliver us from evil.
Radiance of the Father's glory, bringing forth light from light, light of light and fountain of light, day that illuminates the day:
True sun, glide in, shining with everlasting brightness, and pour the radiance of the Holy Spirit into our minds.
With vows let us call upon the Father too, the Father of eternal glory, the Father of mighty grace; may he bind fast the slippery sin.
May he shape our vigorous deeds, blunt the tooth of the envious one, turn harsh misfortunes to good, and give the grace to bear them.
May he steer and direct the mind in a chaste and faithful body; may faith be fervent with heat; may it not know the poison [?] of deceit.
And may Christ be our food, and may our drink be faith; joyful, let us drink the sober drunkenness of the Spirit.
May this day pass by joyfully; may chastity be always like the early morning, faith always like midday; may the mind not know twilight.
The dawn moves its course forward; may the dawn [?] wholly come forth: the Son wholly in the Father, and the Father wholly in the Word.
Creator of eternal light, you yourself are wholly light and day, perceiving no night at all, nature of everlasting light.
Already the pale night gives way to the approaching coming of the day, dulling the light of the stars, and the bright morning star is present.
Already we rise joyfully from our beds, singing thanks also to you, because the sun, the day, returning again, has overcome the blind night.
We pray you now, Holy One, that the pleasures of the flesh may not creep in with flattering heats, and that our mind may not yield to the deceits of the world.
May anger not provoke quarrels, nor gluttony weigh down the belly, nor hunger for wealth overthrow us, nor shameful lust take hold of us.
But with a firm mind, sober, remaining chaste in body, with a wholly faithful spirit, O Christ, let us spend this day.
Creator of the shining heaven, you who set the moon as a light for the nights and the sun for the courses of the days on a sure path.
The black night is now driven away, the brightness of the world is born again, and a new vigor of mind now rouses us to sweet deeds.
The returning day now urges us to sound your praises, and the gentler face of heaven brightens our hearts.
Let us avoid every slipperiness; may the spirit turn away from perverse things; may our deeds not defile our life; may sin not entangle the tongue.
But while the sun completes the day, may deep faith be fervent, may hope call us to the promises, may love join us to Christ.
God of eternal light, beauty beyond words, judge of the coming day, you who see the secrets of the mind.
You hold the kingdom of the heavens, and you are wholly in the Word; you are the Son through all things; you direct all things; you are the fountain of the Holy Spirit.
Threefold name, lofty faith, one, mighty through all things, wondrous also through the sign of the cross, you ruler of immeasurable light.
You are the founder of the world; you sit on the seventh throne as judge; you came down from on high to suffer for us.
You, almighty Lord, keeper of the highest summit, to you belongs wondrous praise, you King, the first resurrection.
You are the helper of faith and of humility; you see [?] for yourself the throne of the high seat; to you also belongs divine glory.
To Christ the eternal and to God the Father, with the Holy Spirit, let us render the gift of life, from ages to ages.
Christ, Lord of heaven, greatest savior of the world, who by the gift of the cross freed us from the laws of death.
Praying to you now, we ask that you preserve your gifts, which you have given universally through the ages to all peoples.
You, Word of the eternal Father, born from the divine mouth, God from God, subsisting, only-begotten Son.
All creation of the world calls you Lord; begun at the Father's command, it was completed by your powers.
To you all the heavenly angels give glory; you the song of the archangels praises with divine voices.
To you the company of the elders, twice twelve in number, bear cups full of fragrant spices, and bowing down they worship you.
To you the cherubim and seraphim, at the seat of the Father's light, sound with unceasing cry and with the beating of six wings:
"Holy, holy, holy, Lord God, Lord forever; heaven and earth are full of your glory."
Save us, Son of David, blessed by the Father, you who come in the name of God, Lord from on high.
You, the spotless Lamb given to the earth as an offering, you who washed the garments of the saints in your blood.
The multitude of the blessed established in heaven, of the witnesses with victories, signs and crowns, follow you, leader of glory.
Add us to their number. We pray to you, Lord: let us sound with one voice, let us praise with one song.
Now that the light of day is restored, with our first voices after sleep let us sing the glory of God, with the help of Christ's grace,
through whom the Creator of all made day and night, decreeing by eternal law that they should always follow one another.
You are the true light of the faithful, whom the old law does not hold; neither does the night follow [?] with its rising, for you shine with eternal light.
Christ, we ask you, grant to your servants who pray that the wickedness of this world may not drive our faith into exile.
Let us not think sinfully; let us envy no one; when injured, let us not pay back in kind; let us overcome evil with good.
Far from our hearts be anger, craftiness and pride; far away be greed, the root of all evils.
Let wine not take hold of the mind through constant drunkenness, but let us drink your cup in a way fitting to our understanding.
Let love that is not feigned keep peace and friendship, and unblemished chastity keep them with constant faith.
To increase [?], let there not be by commands [?] the enticement of gluttony [?], always hunger; where excess [?] ... humility [?], let the psalm of the prophet direct us. [?]
Grant, unbegotten Father, that we may spend this whole day continually pleasing to Christ, filled with the Holy Spirit.
With the morning praises that we sing to the Trinity: "Let us sing again," the true father of the household admonishes.
Let us always be watchful, so that the work of God is not neglected [?], but let us pray continually, as the apostle teaches.
Let us sing to the Lord with the mind; let us sing together also with the spirit. Let the mind not wander among impure things; [?] unwise [?] ... the mind.
But seven times in this day let us speak praise to the Lord; let us give glory to the Godhead, as is our constant duty.
By faith in God, by which we live, with everlasting hope we believe; through the grace [?] of love let us sing the glory of Christ.
He who was led at the third hour to the suffering as a sacrifice, bearing the gallows of the cross, brought back the lost sheep.
Let us therefore pray humbly, set free by redemption, that he may rescue from the world those whom he released from the written bond.
Glory to you, Trinity, equal, one Godhead, both before every age and now and forever.
Keeping a fixed order, let us ask with devout heart, at the third hour of the day, for the glory of the threefold power.
So that we may be a dwelling for the Holy Spirit, who once at this hour was distributed among the apostles.
As this order proceeded, the Creator of the heavenly kingdom adorned all things beautifully, as a reward of eternal life.
Let us speak praise to the Lord with a fervent, eager spirit; the appointed hour, the sixth, calls us to pray.
For in it the true glory of salvation, the sacrifice of the blessed Lamb, is given back to the faithful by the power of the cross.
By its most brilliant light midday grows dark; let us receive with all our heart the grace [?] of so great a radiance.
Having completed the threefold number in the three marks of the hours, singing the praises we owe, saying the ninth hour, let us sing.
Holding the holy mystery of God with a pure heart, by the rule [?] of master Peter, revealed by the sign of salvation.
And let us sing in spirit, clinging to the apostles, who by the power of Christ set right the lame feet.
God, who made the day with bright light, Lord, we ask for your glory while the day sinks and turns away.
Now the sun, as the evening star presses on, goes to its setting, enclosing the world in darkness, keeping its order.
But you, high Lord, [grant] that the quiet night may receive your praying servants, weary from the labor of the day.
So that the day of the world may not pass away from darkened minds, but, covered by your grace, we may see a profitable light.
God, who by fixed laws divide night and day, so that sleep may release bodies weary from cares.
We pray to you in the fearful time of night that, while sleep holds the weary mind, the light of faith may illuminate it.
Let not the cunning enemy entice [us] with wavering cares and pleasures, the secret things of the night, inviting [?] smoothly [?] in this body.
Amid [?] let no terror of anxious fear be in the mind; let it not deceive the mind, nor let the false image of a vision lead it astray.
But when deep sleep binds our cares, may faith, which knows no sleep, never lull the watchful mind to sleep [?].
Christ, you who are light and day, you uncover the darkness of night; you are believed to be the light of light, proclaiming light to the blessed.
We pray, holy Lord, be our protection by night and by day; may we have rest in you; grant a quiet night.
Let no heavy sleep fall upon us, nor the enemy seize us unawares, nor anyone consenting to him make us guilty before you.
Let the eyes take sleep; let the heart always keep watch toward you. May your right hand protect the servants who love you.
Our defender, look on us; hold back those who lie in wait. Guide your servants, whom you have bought with your blood.
Remember us, Lord, in this heavy body. You who are the defender of the soul, be with us, Lord.
At midday we must pray. Christ must be asked to command us to eat of his holy body.
So that he may be praised among all the people, he himself, the Lord of the heavens, who sits in the highest.
May he give us help through wondrous angels, who may always guard us in every life of the world.
Now three times four hours have drawn the day toward evening; the sun is foretelling its setting. The night [?] of the times [?].
So let us, with the sign of the Lord, [?] the breasts of the [?], so that the crafty serpent does not try to find a way in.
But with the weapons of chastity, let the mind, supported and watchful, with free sobriety as its companion, drive back the shameless enemy.
And may no surfeit of food ever bloat our bodies, so that it does not by force, through sleep, defile the deluded soul.
The dawn of light glows red; heaven thunders with praises; the world, rejoicing, exults; hell, groaning, howls.
For the mightiest king, having broken the powers of death and trodden hell underfoot, releases the wretched from their chain.
He who was guarded by soldiers, shut in by the stone, rises from death as victor, triumphing in noble splendour.
The groans and the pains of hell are now undone, for the Lord has risen, the shining angel cries.
The apostles were sad at the slaying of their Lord, whom the wicked servants condemned to the cruel punishment of death.
With a gentle word the angel told the women in advance: "In Galilee the Lord is to be seen, quickly."
As they hurry to tell this to the apostles, they see him alive and kiss the feet of the Lord.
When the disciples learn this, they go at once to Galilee to see the longed-for face of the Lord.
In the bright Easter joy the sun shines with a pure ray, when the apostles now see Christ with bodily sight.
The wounds were shown to them in Christ's shining flesh, and they declare with a loud voice that the Lord has risen.
Christ, most gracious king, take possession of our hearts, so that we may give you the praise we owe at all times.
To God the Father be glory, and to his only Son, with the burning Spirit, both now and forever.
This is the true day of God, holy and bright with light, on which the holy blood washed away the shameful, unchaste crimes of the world.
It pours faith into the unbelieving and gives light and sight to the blind. Whom does the thief's pardon not release from heavy fear?
He exchanged the cross for a reward and sought the Saviour with a brief faith. Righteous, going ahead by a step, he came into the kingdom of God.
The angels too are astonished, seeing the punishment in the body, and the guilty man clinging to Christ, seizing blessed life.
A wondrous mystery: that it washes away the impurity of the world, takes away the sins of all, flesh cleansing the vices of the flesh.
What can be higher than this: that sin seeks grace, and love releases fear, and death gives back new life?
Let death swallow the hook for itself and bind itself in its own knots; let the life of all die, let the life of all rise again.
When death passes over all, all the dead rise again; death, consumed by its own blow, may lament that it alone has perished.
At the supper of the Lamb, made ready, shining in white garments, after the crossing of the Red Sea, let us sing to Christ the Prince.
His holy body was roasted on the altar of the cross; by tasting his rose-red blood we live to God.
Protected on the evening of Easter from the destroying angel, rescued from the most powerful command of Pharaoh.
Now Christ is our Easter, who is the slain lamb; his body is offered as the unleavened bread of purity.
O truly worthy sacrifice, through which hell is broken, the captive people redeemed, and the rewards of life given back.
Then Christ rises from the grave mightily; victorious, he returned [?] from the pit of hell, binding the tyrant of evil with a bond and unlocking the garden of delight.
We pray you, Author of all, in this Easter joy, protect your people from every onslaught of death.
The eternal gifts of Christ and the victories of the martyrs, bringing due praise, let us sing with joyful minds.
Princes of the churches and triumphant leaders of war, warriors of the heavenly hall, and true lights of the world.
Having conquered the terror of the world and scorned the punishments of the body, through the shortcut of a holy death they possess blessed life.
The martyrs are handed over to fire and to the teeth of wild beasts; armed with claws, the hands of the mad torturer rage.
Their bared entrails hang; the hallowed blood is poured out; but they remain unmoved, by the grace of eternal life.
The devoted faith of the saints, the unconquered hope of believers, the perfect love of Christ has triumphed over the prince of the world.
In them the Father's glory, in them the will of the Spirit rejoices, in them the Son; heaven is filled with joy.
You now, Redeemer, we pray, that you join your praying servants to the fellowship of the martyrs, forever and ever.
At the time of the night, rising, saying praise to God, to Christ, Christ [?] and Lord, in the glory of the Trinity.
Let us sing a holy chant [?], bow our necks, bend our knees to the earth, and lay ourselves down, confessing our sins.
Let us always pray to God to make amends for evil with good, and with the fruit of repentance always to fulfill our vows.
Let us pray to Christ and the holy Father, and the Spirit of the Father, that he may give us help to overcome the host of the envious enemy.
Eternal King, Lord, Creator of all things, you who are before the ages, always the Son with the Father.
You who at the beginning of the world created Adam, the man, to whom you gave a face like your own image;
whom the devil, the enemy of the human race, had deceived; whose bodily form you deigned to take on;
so that you might redeem the man whom you had created long before, so that you might join us to God through the fellowship of the flesh;
whom, born of a virgin, every soul fears; through whom we believe with devoted mind that we shall rise again;
you who through baptism gave us forgiveness, we who were held there, bound in the bonds of conscience;
you who for the sake of man deigned to take up the cross, you gave your blood as the price of our salvation.
For the veil of the temple was torn, and all the earth trembled; then you awakened many of those who were sleeping, Lord.
You crush the powers of the ancient enemy through the cross of death, by which we, marked on our foreheads, carry the banner of victory of the faith.
May you deign always to drive him away from us, so that he may never be able to harm those redeemed by your blood.
You who for our sake deigned to descend to hell, so that you might give the gifts of life to the debtors of death.
To you in the night-time, weeping, we sing praise: forgive us, Lord, forgive those who confess.
For you yourself are witness and judge, whom no one can deceive, seeing the hidden traces of our conscience.
You alone are the searcher of our hearts; you are the good physician who stands by our hidden wounds.
You are the one who at a fixed time will give an end to the world; you are the just rewarder of the merits of all.
Therefore, Holy One, we pray you to cleanse our wounds, you who are the Son with the Father, always with the Holy Spirit.
Eternal founder of things, who rules night and day, and gives the times their seasons so that you may relieve weariness:
the herald of the day already sounds, keeping watch through the deep night, a night-light for travellers, separating night from night.
Awakened by him, the morning star frees the sky from darkness; at him every band of wanderers abandons the path of doing harm.
At him the sailor gathers his strength, and the straits of the sea grow calm; at his singing the very rock of the Church washes away sin.
Let us therefore rise up quickly: the cock wakes those lying down and rebukes the sleepy; the cock reproves those who deny.
When the cock sings, hope is raised up again, health is poured back into the sick, the thief's weapon is unbound [?], faith returns to the fallen.
Saviour, look upon those who are afraid, and by looking upon us correct us; if you look upon us, the fallen do not fall, and sin is loosed by weeping.
You, light, shine upon our minds, and shake off the sleep of the night; let our voice sound to you first, and let us render our mouths to you.
We praise you, God; we acknowledge you as Lord; you, eternal Father, all the earth worships.
To you all the angels, to you the heavens and all the powers, to you the cherubim and seraphim cry out with unceasing voice.
Holy, holy, holy, Lord God, Lord of hosts; heaven and earth are full of the majesty of your glory.
You the glorious choir of the apostles, you the praiseworthy number of the prophets, you the shining army of the martyrs praises.
You the holy congregation confesses throughout the circle of the earth: the Father of boundless majesty, your venerable, true, only Son, and also the Holy Spirit, the Comforter.
You, Christ, are the King of glory; you are the everlasting Son of the Father; you, when you took on man to set him free, did not shrink from the virgin's womb.
You, having [?] overcome the sting of death, opened the kingdom of the heavens to believers.
You sit at the right hand of God, in the glory of the Father; we believe that you will come as judge.
Therefore we ask you: help your servants, whom you redeemed with precious blood.
Make them be rewarded with eternal glory among your saints.
Lord, save your people and bless your inheritance; rule them and lift them up for ever.
Day by day we bless you, and we praise your name for ever, for ever and ever.
Lord, be pleased to keep us without sin this day.
[?] us, Lord, [?] us.
Lord, let your mercy be upon us, as we have hoped in you.
In you, Lord, I have hoped; let me never be put to shame.
